Check: git hash-object treasuryV3Listen.ts treasuryAddresses.ts must print the two blob hashes above.
Pinned generator dependency: ethers 6.17.0 (package-lock.json). Its transitive packages include ws,
which ethers loads for its WebSocket provider class. This fixture generator never creates a
WebSocket connection; it only encodes logs and parses them. Recorded as an indirect dependency.

Offline boundary:
- Installing the pinned dependency needs `npm ci` in this directory, which reads the npm registry
  (https://registry.npmjs.org) or an npm cache that already holds the locked tarballs.
- On a fresh offline machine, either pre-fill the npm cache with these locked versions before
  running `npm ci`, or replace the dependency with a vendored copy of the locked ethers tree.
- The 444579d regeneration was reproduced with `npm ci --offline` (dependencies from the local npm
  cache), with the script asserting ethers 6.17.0. The lockfile was also checked offline with
  `npm ls --package-lock-only --all`.

isMiner fixture (tests/fixtures/treasury_v3_isminer.json):
- Generator: gen-isminer-fixtures.mjs in this directory. It reads treasuryV3Listen.ts (blob
  014febd8b30b8a64bc5397a6d3ae7dc4055f7c9e, checked), finds the ABI line
  `function isMiner(address account) view returns (bool)` exactly once, and encodes and decodes with
  ethers 6.17.0 from package-lock.json.
- Scope: calldata and return-data decoding and the strict bool rule only. No vote is built and no
  signer is involved. The treasury deployment address is not verified here; the Rust test uses an
  address only as a stub argument.
- Reproduce with `npm ci --offline` in this directory, then
  `node --no-warnings gen-isminer-fixtures.mjs --out <path>`.
